visualVerdict.lowCatches: Both mirrored cancelled-dive catches preserve their exact initial deformed mesh, gather the solved ball and rise from hip 0.300 to 0.830 m. The rise finishes by the 1.542 s sample, then remains settled; baseline remains squatting. Fixed ankle x/z anchors do not slide.
visualVerdict.compressedControls: Both candidates remain byte-identical to their completed authored source throughout 0–3 s, retaining low ankles and flat-sole metadata. Baseline re-enters later stance/arm changes, finishing by 1.958 and 2.542 s. Candidate intentionally preserves the asymmetric low-hand end stance rather than introducing a new centered ready-hands idle.
visualVerdict.handsAndFeet: Matched enlarged crops show actual fingers and distal thumb cup around the solved caught ball, and retained foot anchors through the rise. Angular cuff/inner-elbow silhouettes remain; no remesh improvement is claimed.
visualVerdict.framing: Same frozen camera is used before/after each whole sequence. Every extended 0–3 s vertex is verified to fit. Enlarged crops use same paired per-time cameras and do not re-pose or reshape geometry.

interpretation.normalSpeed: All exports contain result elapsed 0 through 3.0 s at 24 fps. Normal playback assigns one frame per 1/24 s, including the displayed endpoint; encoded duration 73/24=3.041667 s.
interpretation.quarterSpeed: Same ordered source frames at 6 source frames/s (4x longer), encoded at 24 fps by repeating each source frame four times. Repetition is exact; there is no invented motion interpolation. The source was not resampled at 96 Hz. Slowed playback exposes these sampled states but provides no continuous-time smoothness or collision proof; normal-speed ordered-frame review and the separate dense numeric gates remain the motion evidence.
interpretation.deduplication: Only byte-identical full mesh buffers share offline render images; all 73 chronological frames remain in each final clip.

limitations: Offline CPU-skinned geometry with simplified materials; not gameplay, browser/WebGL, phone, or GPU proof.
Angular cuff edges remain; pose and contact evidence is not force-balance or full physical dynamics validation.
24 fps visual sampling does not establish continuous collision freedom. Separate geometry/lifecycle tests belong to the integration receipt.
Inherited actual-skin minima are +18.05 mm for the caught cases and +8.55 mm for the compressed controls; fixed ankle anchors do not prove weight-bearing sole contact.

The two free-control balls finish far outside the character view (x=29.34 m and 34.12 m) and are omitted from the close geometry render. Exact terminal points remain in metadata; caught balls use the actual keeperGather solution in every frame.
Four-sample whole-body views retain visible offline noise; enlarged hand/foot views use sixteen samples. No browser textures, shaders, WebGL, phone GPU, or device-frame-time validation is implied.

additionalGloveReview.visualClassification: Localized glove compression with a small pre-existing surface intersection; no obvious finger passing through the opposite palm in these views. A tiny highlighted sliver is visible from the ball-facing side. The faces are hidden behind the glove surface from the opposite side. This is not a zero-intersection claim.

finalSourceCompatibility.note: Original rendered evidence and hashes remain unchanged. The only final source change is inspector-only motion-lab-runtime.js. Re-exporting the final candidate plus frozen baseline reproduces all original 584 skin buffers, joints, ball points, recipes and captures exactly.
